items.title: METR Q4 2026 capability update: AI R&D-relevant capabilities improving fast but getting harder to measure
items.summary_en: METR's update covers models up to Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. According to the search-result description, it reports that models do worse on tasks that are costlier to turn into training environments, and that time horizons double about every 3.6 months. The title says measurement of these capabilities is becoming harder.
items.notes: metr.org could not be fetched (host not resolvable in this session). Content comes from a web search result description of the METR page, not from reading the full page. Figures such as the 3.6-month doubling time and the model names must be checked against the original before publication. Methodology caveats stated by METR could not be read.

items.title: METR note: Measuring alignment eval tells
items.summary_en: A METR note by Uzay Girit, Kaivu Hariharan and Leni Shor. According to the search-result description, it finds that investigator agents increasingly distinguish alignment evals from capability evals, often by spotting environments that look fake.
items.notes: Published 2 days before the nominal window starts (2026-11-18). It is included because the previous run was 2026-08-29. Notes are likely less formal than full reports, but METR's own caveats were not read. The summary comes from a search snippet.

items.title: METR independent assessment of AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic, October 2026
items.summary_en: According to the search-result description, METR estimates that Anthropic's capability progress on well-specified tasks is roughly twice its pre-October 2025 pace, with high uncertainty. It attributes most of the speedup to Anthropic's own use of AI in R&D and reports no convincing bottlenecks over the next 12 months. The public version is redacted.
items.notes: Outside the nominal window; included as a significant item since the last run. The public version has redactions and METR's full report includes a redacted forecast. The search result states the uncertainty is high. The page was not read directly. Note the assessment evaluates Anthropic's own AI R&D, so check how it relates to Anthropic's own statements, which belong to the industry collector.

items.title: METR review of the 'Risks from automated R&D' section in Anthropic's August 2026 Risk Report
items.summary_en: An external review by METR that, per the search-result description, compares Anthropic's public and private risk report language on AI-driven acceleration. METR is described as judging the risk level 'low' for the models available at the time.
items.notes: Outside the nominal window. Page not read; the 'low' risk judgement comes from a search snippet and needs verification. Read together with the Anthropic acceleration assessment published the same day.
